chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who accused a group of people collectively, so he flogged him with one limit (hadd). The explanation in this report is one of two things: One is that we interpret it according to the detail contained in the first report, that only one limit was obligatory upon him if they came to him together, but if they came separately, it would be obligatory upon him for each person a limit according to the complete report. The second explanation is that we interpret it as: if he accused them with one word, he is obligated one limit, but if he accused them with different words, he is obligated for each person a limit, which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for accusing multiple people of zina in one go?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s resolution to the apparent contradiction in Amir al-Mu'minin’s ruling by distinguishing between the manner of accusation (single phrase vs. distinct words) and the manner of presentation (simultaneous vs. separate). This juristic nuance highlights the Shia emphasis on contextual interpretation (ta'wil) in applying the hadd of qadhf, ensuring legal precision in cases involving multiple defendants. The ruling underscores the principle that the number of lashes corresponds to the distinctness of the accusation rather than merely the number of accused parties.
